Ater
ā'ter
n. (the head of a family called Ater of Hezekiah, ninety and eight of whom returned from the captivity; also the head of a house of the porters)
From Hebrew 'Ater, from 'atar, to shut up or bind — hence shut up, lame, or left-handed, since the related idiom describes a man bound in his right hand. Two distinct houses bear the name in the register: Ater of Hezekiah among the people, and Ater among the porters.

Biblical Definition

Ater is remembered by a phrase that has puzzled readers for centuries: “The children of Ater of Hezekiah, ninety and eight” (Ezr 2:16), repeated exactly in Nehemiah's roll (Neh 7:21). Whether Hezekiah was a further ancestor, or the family claimed descent from the good king of Judah, the register does not explain — and its unwillingness to explain is characteristic. Ezra copies what the record said. A second Ater heads a house of gatekeepers: “The children of the porters: the children of Shallum, the children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub” (Ezr 2:42), a hundred and thirty-nine doorkeepers in all. And Ater sealed the covenant with the chief of the people: “Ater, Hizkijah, Azzur” (Neh 10:17), where Hizkijah is the Hebrew of the same name as Hezekiah, standing next to him in the list. Ninety-eight people is a very small house. They are written down anyway, twice, with a note attached that nobody can now fully explain, because they were there.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Ater; in sacred history he is the head of a family called Ater of Hezekiah, and of a house of the porters, in the register of the return.

ATER, n. Shut up, bound; the head of a family of the children of Israel.

The children of Ater of Hezekiah were ninety and eight in the register of the return.

The same number is given in the parallel roll in Nehemiah.

A house of the porters is also called the children of Ater.

Ater is named among those that sealed the covenant in the days of Nehemiah.

Key Scripture

Ezr 2:16 — "The children of Ater of Hezekiah, ninety and eight."

Neh 7:21 — "The children of Ater of Hezekiah, ninety and eight."

Ezr 2:42 — "The children of the porters: the children of Shallum, the children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub, the children of Hatita, the children of Shobai, in all an hundred thirty and nine."

Neh 10:17 — "Ater, Hizkijah, Azzur,"

Modern Corruption

There is no significant modern redefinition of this name. The principle to recover is that a faithful record keeps what it does not understand, and that a Bible edited down to what its editors could explain would be a smaller and a poorer book.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Ater is a family head in a census and nobody has contested him. What the phrase Ater of Hezekiah sets before the reader is the honesty of the register. A compiler tidying his sources would have dropped or explained an obscure qualifier; Ezra transcribes it and moves on, and Nehemiah's independent copy has it too. The same is true across Scripture: unexplained names, unresolved details, hard sayings left standing. The text bears every mark of having been received rather than composed.

The principle to recover is the sufficiency and the honesty of Scripture together. “The secret things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law” (Deu 29:29). There is a great deal in the Bible a careful reader cannot fully account for — and the response of faith is neither to pretend the difficulty away nor to cut the passage out, but to do the words that are plain. Ninety-eight souls from a house whose second name nobody can now explain went home to Jerusalem, and God had their number written down.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Ater (H333), Ater; 'atar (H332), to shut up, bind; Chizqiyah (H2396), Hezekiah, Hizkijah; sho'er (H7778), porter, gatekeeper; sepher hayyachas (H5612 with H3188), the book of the genealogy.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Ater (H333) — Ater; the head of two houses in the register.

Hebrew 'atar (H332) — to shut up, to bind; the root of the name.

Hebrew Chizqiyah (H2396) — Hezekiah; the qualifier attached to his house.

Hebrew sho'er (H7778) — porter; the other Ater's office.

Hebrew yachas (H3188) — genealogy, the reckoning by descent.

Usage

"“The children of Ater of Hezekiah, ninety and eight” — a phrase preserved without explanation."

"“The children of the porters… the children of Ater” — a second house of the same name."

"“Ater, Hizkijah, Azzur” — the two names side by side on the sealed covenant."
